newsitem.title: ITALY: Spain to get small extension of telecoms deadline.
newsitem.headline: Spain to get small extension of telecoms deadline.

text.p: Spain is to get only a strictly limited exemption from having to adopt EU legislation to open its telecommunications market to full competition next year, EU Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Monday.

Van Miert told the transport committee of the lower house of parliament that alliances between Spanish telecoms operator Telefonica de Espana SA and British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp had given Telefonica access to overseas markets while its home market was still relatively closed.

The European Union has set January 1, 1998 as a deadline for opening up the continent's telecommunications industry to competition but has already granted Ireland, Portugal and Luxembourg more time to open up their markets fully.
Van Miert said he would propose temporary exemptions for Greece and Spain in the coming weeks.
"For Spain I want to propose that there will be a very circumscribed derogation (exemption)," Van miert said.

"We have asked that before granting a derogation of limited scope that Spain should also open its market as soon as possible ... in the course of next year Spain will have to open its telecommunications market to competition," he said.

"This is because Telefonica has already concluded an alliance with other partners, and it therefore has access to other markets that are open to it while the Spanish market is still relatively closed," he added.
